_meta.note: Figures the page uses that do not live on FRED. Every entry carries a source, a URL, a tier and an as-of date, and is mirrored in docs/THESIS.md (sections 'September 2026 update', 'update II' and 'Update III (23 Sep 2026)'). TIER 1 = official statistics, central banks, IEA, IMF, WTO, Fed research. TIER 2 = Reuters, Bloomberg, FT, CNBC, S&P Global, Lloyd's List, Kpler, major outlets. TIER 3 is never load-bearing and does not appear here.
_meta.rule: If a figure here disagrees with a FRED series in the snapshot, the FRED series wins and this entry must be corrected.
_meta.superseded: An entry replaced by a newer reading keeps its key, because older views (the V4 ledger) read it by name, and gains `superseded_by` naming the key that replaces it. Read the newer key for anything current.

fed_counterpoint.name: Why gold did not actually overtake Treasuries as the world's favourite reserve asset
fed_counterpoint.author: Colin Weiss, Federal Reserve Board
fed_counterpoint.finding: The crossover is a valuation effect driven by private ETF demand since late 2024, not central bank accumulation; by June 2026 foreign official Treasury holdings again exceeded world gold reserves excluding the US in dollar terms. Five legacy holders (US, Germany, Italy, France, IMF) own 52% of official gold and have not added since the 1970s. Foreign officials bought roughly USD 200bn of Treasuries net between 2022 and April 2026.

mines_cleared.president_claim: all mines have been removed from the Strait of Hormuz
mines_cleared.note: OFFICIAL CLAIMS, labelled as such. The President announced that all mines had been removed. Two US officials with direct knowledge told Axios the Navy had cleared the Traffic Separation Scheme (the median shipping lane between Oman and Iran), and that over several months US Navy underwater drones had located more than 100 objects suspected to be mines, with private contractors hired to remove or detonate them. Bloomberg reported on 26 Aug that US allies cast doubt on the claim that the strait had been demined. Transits did not recover: IMF PortWatch counted four vessels on 25 Aug.
mines_cleared.source: Axios, 25 August 2026, citing two US officials; Bloomberg, 26 August 2026

september_escalation.note: CENTCOM said US forces destroyed five Iranian tankers late on Tuesday 8 Sep after the IRGC fired ballistic missiles at a US Navy warship twice in two days; crews were warned to abandon ship first. Iran fired 20 ballistic missiles at a US base near Al Azraq, Jordan; Jordan's armed forces said 18 were intercepted and two fell in unpopulated areas, with no casualties. The IRGC's claim to have attacked 10 ships (two American vessels, eight tankers) is Iran's own and was not independently verified.
september_escalation.source: Al Jazeera, 9 September 2026, citing CENTCOM and the Jordanian Armed Forces; Euronews, 9 September 2026

east_west_pipeline.note: Saudi Arabia's 1,200 km East-West pipeline, which carries crude from the Gulf coast to Yanbu on the Red Sea and so bypasses Hormuz, was shut on Thursday 10 Sep after an attack Saudi Arabia blamed on drones from Iranian-backed militias in Iraq. Two regional officials told AP repairs could take three to five weeks and that the line might work partially meanwhile. It resumed operations on 22 Sep at a lower pumping rate (The National, 23 Sep). Capacity is AP's 'up to 7 million barrels of oil a day'; how much was flowing at the time of the attack is not given by AP and is not recorded here.
east_west_pipeline.source: Associated Press via PBS NewsHour, 14 September 2026; The National, 23 September 2026

tankers_21_sep.note: UKMTO reported a crude tanker entering the strait hit by an 'unknown projectile' (two crew with minor injuries) and an outbound LPG carrier hit by debris from unknown projectiles (no casualties). Neither UKMTO nor France 24 attributed the attacks.

us_iran_talks.iran_claim: Iran could reopen Hormuz within seven days if the US eased military pressure and lifted its blockade
us_iran_talks.note: CUTS AGAINST the escalation reading, and the market treated it that way: Brent futures fell below $100 (see prices.crude_spot_vs_futures). Accounts of the format differ: US envoy Witkoff said mediators 'shuttled between' delegations; the President described a three-hour meeting; Iranian state media reported a meeting between Foreign Minister Araghchi and Witkoff. Al Jazeera describes it as following weeks without direct contact. The seven-day reopening offer is a senior Iranian official speaking to Reuters and is a claim; Iran's stated conditions include lifting the naval blockade and unfreezing assets.

crude_spot_vs_futures.name: Crude, September 2026: physical spot vs front-month futures

spot.source: US EIA spot prices via FRED DCOILBRENTEU (Europe Brent spot FOB) and DCOILWTICO (Cushing, OK)

crude_spot_vs_futures.note: Both sets of numbers are real; they are different instruments. The ICE Brent futures contract settled $108.75 on 15 Sep while EIA's Brent spot series printed $130.80 the same day: a $22 physical premium, the same kind of paper-physical gap the IEA recorded in April (a record $35 then). After five losing sessions on news of US-Iran talks, Brent FUTURES settled $99.25 on 22 Sep, below $100, but Brent SPOT was still $114.89. 'Oil below $100' is true of futures only. WTI spot peaked at $107.02 on 15 Sep, below the $114.58 war peak of 7 Apr. The page's price series is FRED spot; never mix the two in one line.

aircraft.note: Three F-15Es were lost to friendly fire over Kuwait on 2 March; five KC-135s were damaged on the ground at Prince Sultan Air Base on 14 March; two MC-130Js were destroyed in Iran during the 5 April rescue. Count is as of the CRS report and will be updated from any later official tally. UPDATE 23 Sep 2026: CBO (15 Sep) also counts 42 planes plus one radar system lost through 1 August, so the headline 42 stands. The DoD Lead Inspector General's quarterly report on Operation Epic Fury (released 9 Sep, covering to 30 Jun) gives 'as many as 30' MQ-9s destroyed (CRS: 24) and adds four AH-6s, an AH-64 and an MH-60S not in the CRS list; its counts are 'at least' / 'as many as' ranges, so by_type is NOT changed to mix the two sources (Al Jazeera, 15 Sep, summarising the IG report; IG report https://media.defense.gov/2026/Sep/09/2003993626/-1/-1/1/OEF_Q3_JUN2026_FINAL_508%20SECURE.PDF).

bases.note: Iran struck the Navy's Bahrain logistics hub on the first day. Regional ports large enough for a carrier remain inside missile range, so supply ships sail to Diego Garcia and the fleet resupplies at sea every five to six days. USS Abraham Lincoln spent about nine months deployed without a port call before USS George Washington relieved it on 20 August.

munitions.denial: Defense Secretary Hegseth disputed the reports (5 August); the President demanded answers on the shortages (3 September).

CNN reported about 80% of THAAD and half of Patriot stocks used. The $21bn munitions line in the supplemental is consistent with the estimates the Secretary disputes. No newer Tier 1/2 Patriot count found as of 23 Sep. CBO (15 Sep) separately estimates the US has probably used between one-half and two-thirds of its inventory of certain interceptors since June 2025 and that rebuilding would probably take at least five years (see war_cost.cbo_estimate).
